docs.title: SportsLabResearch FIFA World Cup 2026 Analytics
docs.text:
Scientific software for acquisition, organization and analysis of FIFA World Cup 2026 data.

SportsLabResearch-FIFA-World-Cup-2026-Analytics is an open research software project designed to retrieve, structure, document and analyze official FIFA World Cup 2026 information.

docs.title: Main capabilities
docs.text:
• Complete player statistics
  • Complete team statistics
  • Combined player and team datasets
  • Official squad information
  • Player date of birth
  • Variable dictionary included in exported Excel files
  • Complementary FIFA World Cup 2026 information
  • Automated Excel outputs
  • Reproducible research workflow

docs.title: Main menu
docs.text:
1. Download complete player statistics
  2. Download complete team statistics
  3. Download players + teams
  4. Complementary FIFA information
  5. Audit
  6. Exit

docs.title: Scientific scope
docs.text:
The open-source core is designed to support reproducible research on:

  • Relative Age Effect in elite football.
  • Player selection and tournament participation.
  • Associations between age, position, club and national team.
  • Transparent baseline predictive modelling.
  • Reusable tournament datasets and scientific reports.

The first public case study will use a FIFA World Cup dataset. The architecture is intentionally tournament-independent.

docs.title: Data Acquisition
docs.text: The acquisition workflow retrieves and integrates official FIFA World Cup 2026 information.

docs.title: General workflow
docs.text:
1. Identify the FIFA resource
  2. Retrieve available information
  3. Validate the expected population
  4. Normalize fields and values
  5. Integrate complementary sources
  6. Export structured datasets

docs.title: Reference population
docs.text:
• 1,248 players
  • 48 national teams

Validation mechanisms detect incomplete downloads before final export.

docs.title: Data Processing
docs.text: Retrieved data are processed before export to generate analysis-ready datasets.

docs.title: Main operations
docs.text:
• Character cleaning
  • Field normalization
  • Player identification
  • Team identification
  • Statistical category integration
  • Variable harmonization
  • Date processing
  • Derived birth variables
  • Dataset merging
  • Excel-safe export

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text: The project is specifically designed for the FIFA World Cup 2026.

docs.title: Primary sources
docs.text:
• FIFA player statistics
  • FIFA team statistics
  • Official squad lists
  • Tournament information
  • Competition standings
  • Match information
  • FIFA Power Rankings

The software is not currently designed for other FIFA competitions.

docs.title: Does the software work with other FIFA tournaments?
docs.text: No. Version 0.7.6 is specifically designed for the FIFA World Cup 2026.

docs.title: Does it include player dates of birth?
docs.text: Yes.

docs.title: How many players are expected?
docs.text: 1,248 players from 48 national teams.

docs.title: Are the variables documented?
docs.text: Yes. Generated Excel workbooks include a variable dictionary.

docs.title: Is an internet connection required?
docs.text: Yes. FIFA information is retrieved from online resources.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Windows
  • Python 3.11 or later
  • Internet connection
  • Google Chrome

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text: The software is specifically designed around the structure and availability of FIFA World Cup 2026 information.

docs.title: Important limitations
docs.text:
• FIFA may modify website structure or endpoints.
  • Some variables may not be available for all players.
  • Statistical categories may contain different numbers of valid observations.
  • External web changes may require future software updates.
  • The software is not currently validated for other FIFA tournaments.

Researchers should retain the software version and acquisition date used in each study.
